source_context: GDT181 imported_unreviewed; this review scopes its conditional P7 prediction only.
prediction: A one-layer phoneme substitution should fail unless compiler coordinates are modeled.
tested_scope: GDT188 fixed one-to-one glyph substitution against frozen fifteenth-century and medical Latin structural controls.
GDT189 compiler-stripped injective named-letter mappings over six historical language packs and matched anonymous KT.
GDT190 fixed frequent whole-word PAGE_HOST nomenclators (K=8,16,32,64).
GDT191 context-keyed nomenclators at global, Currier, section, hand, and physical-folio scopes.
GDT192 one/two-letter emissions for 20 PAGE_HOST signs under six packs.
GDT193 vowel-deleted consonantal maps and GDT194 fixed consonantal homophony.

adjudication.result: P7 is supported as a bounded negative architectural prediction: these tested one-layer or compiler-stripped families lose to matched source models or leave the frozen structural gap unchanged.
adjudication.meaningful_outcome: The failures support retaining compiler/context conditioning as necessary for these tested simple families; they do not show that a compiler-conditioned phoneme cipher is sufficient, nor identify a language, cipher, plaintext, or phoneme inventory.
invalid_overreach: generic impossibility of all ciphers or languages
rejection of Latin plaintext in general
proof that the hybrid compiler is the true generator
translation or semantic binding from decoder labels
adjudication.controls_vs_manuscript: GDT188 is a structural control result; GDT189-194 are bounded decoder/model failures. They should not be merged into a universal manuscript-language verdict.
adjudication.reopen_or_decisive_test: A genuinely predeclared compiler-conditioned phoneme model would need held manuscript targets, fixed coordinates and an explicit rival/null, then improve a held objective while preserving stability and provide an independently grounded content contrast. Merely adding more keys, contexts, or post-hoc mappings is insufficient.

prior_scope_check: Existing hf_root_scoped_question_draft concerns broad formal hybrid architecture and explicitly warns that rejected compact policies do not refute every cipher/language model; this HN review is narrower and conditional on P7.

evidence.quote:
A fixed one-to-one substitution only renames symbols.  It cannot change the
GDT003/GDT159 operation inventory, transformation rectangles, LEFT×RIGHT
compatibility graph, compatible-pair density, or GDT160 pairing excess.
Therefore the frozen historical Latin controls remain where they are after
*any* Foxton-like glyph renaming.

Do not search for a single Foxton/Fontana-style character key on the visible
Voynich text.  If a historical language lies underneath, at least one
additional nonbijective layer—abbreviation, context-dependent rendering,
nomenclator/codebook behavior, or the independently observed record
compiler—must be removed first.  This is a useful architectural exclusion,
not a language identification.

The result does not reject every Latin plaintext, every scientific cipher, or
the broader GDT181 hybrid.  It closes the direct fixed-bijection route for the
frozen Latin comparators.  No glyph value, sound, word, language, plaintext,

The experiment scores the visible groups, wrapper/DY-stripped residual hosts,
and full PAGE_HOST layer under the same six historical language packs and a
matched anonymous order-2 KT control.  PAGE_HOST contains 60023
events on 2430 physical lines with
20 active signs.

The frozen PAGE_HOST layer was treated as an opaque nomenclator rather than a
letter stream.  For each K in 8, 16, 32, and 64, the K most frequent hosts were
mapped bijectively to the K most frequent words of each of six frozen
historical-language packs and scored with an order-1 word model.  Rare hosts
reset the mapped run, and the matched source-identity KT model sees exactly the
same 5108 events and 3490 runs for the
winning K.

The global K=8 PAGE_HOST nomenclator was expanded into five fixed key scopes:
global, Currier, section, hand, and physical folio. Every stratum selected its
own top eight hosts (or fewer when necessary), paid its complete permutation
key, and was compared with an independently integrated source-identity KT
channel on the same mapped events.

The most flexible physical-folio model is also the closest result: `middle_high_german`
on 93 strata and 6333 mapped events, but it
still loses **240.070 bits**
(0.0379 bits/event), and the complete decoder is
not stable across three starts.

Each of the 20 active PAGE_HOST source signs was allowed to emit any
one- or two-letter string under all six frozen historical-language packs. The
search was nested from the three exact GDT189 mappings and exhaustively tested
all 702 emissions for every sign until one-coordinate local optimality. The
code pays the full mapping, expansion-boundary sequence, and reverse ambiguity.

The direction is worth retaining as architectural evidence: vowel omission is
less incompatible with PAGE_HOST than literal alphabetic text. It is not a
language or phonetic result, because the paid channel still loses by tens of
thousands of bits and supplies no stable key. Any viable skeleton theory needs
context-dependent restoration or a different unit, not this static alphabet.

Fixed consonantal homophony is therefore another insufficient substrate. The
vowel-omission direction survives only as an architectural hint; it supplies no
consonant values or language identification.

No sign, sound, word, language, plaintext, meaning, or translation is
established. Every f84 row was rejected before parsing or scoring.
